summary.oneLiner: TIL positions itself as an 80-year-old Indian material handling and infrastructure equipment leader transforming into a diversified, indigenous capital goods engineering group spanning material handling, defence and clean energy through the acquisition of Tulip Compression (TCPL).
summary.business: TIL Limited designs, manufactures and services mobile cranes (truck cranes, rough terrain cranes, pick-and-carry cranes), ReachStackers, high-capacity forklift trucks and specialised defence equipment from two integrated plants in West Bengal - Kamarhati (Kolkata) and Kharagpur. It sells under its own brand and, through long-standing alliances, distributes and manufactures Manitowoc/Grove cranes and Hyster lift trucks and port-handling systems in India, Nepal and Bhutan. Customers span ports, ICDs and container freight stations, construction and infrastructure contractors, mining/oil/petroleum, railways and the Indian Armed Forces, supported by an aftermarket business covering spares, AMCs, rebuilds and on-site service.

Mobile cranes: CarryKing 515 (pick-and-carry on-deck crane, 360 degree continuous slew)

currentContext.expansion: TIL's FY26 expansion story is about reviving and broadening its two existing West Bengal plants rather than adding a new site. Rough Terrain Cranes, previously manufactured exclusively at Kamarhati, are now also produced at Kharagpur - a deliberate diversification to improve production flexibility, delivery reliability and operational resilience; Kharagpur's stated primary products now include Rough Terrain Cranes 'from FY25'. A capacity utilisation programme run with IIM Mumbai evaluates standard man-hours, work content, skill utilisation, asset usage and workflow streamlining, and its insights are being embedded into daily production rhythms; a new incentive scheme, based on an IIM Mumbai-recommended framework, was launched from April 2026 to replace the legacy scheme. Tripartite Change of Domicile agreements were completed for both the Kamarhati and Kharagpur facilities. A newly revamped administrative office was commissioned at Kharagpur in FY26, SAP (ERP) integration is in process across facilities, and a WMS is live at the Dankuni warehouse. The Kharagpur plant houses a 1 MW rooftop solar plant meeting approximately 90% of that plant's energy requirements at less than 50% of state grid power cost. Product-side expansion runs through the three EXCON 2025 launches (CarryKing 515, RT RST-8, TMS 885) now at customer sites, a pipeline of new retail-sector products over the next two years, higher-capacity cranes in the 110T-300T+ range, enhanced Rough Terrain and Truck Crane variants (110T-130T), next-generation container handling including advanced Empty Container Handlers, and new upgraded variants targeted for launch by FY28. Inorganic expansion came from the acquisition of 60% of Tulip Compression Private Limited from Gainwell Commosales Private Limited - approved by shareholders at the EGM of 14th March 2026 and effective 7th May 2026, making TCPL a material subsidiary - which takes TIL into LNG, CNG and Hydrogen compression and dispensing systems. Geographic expansion is targeted at EMEA, Asia-Pacific, Southeast Asia, GCC, Australia and New Zealand. Funding: the Company raised paid-up capital through share warrants convertible into equity of up to Rs 60 crore issued to promoter TIL Global Private Limited, with proceeds earmarked for growth initiatives including capital expenditure for growth including acquisition, working capital and general corporate purposes.

risks.risk: Qualified audit opinion on the recoverability of deferred tax assets
risks.note: The statutory auditors qualified their opinion on Note 10.2: as of 31 March 2026 the Company carried Deferred Tax Assets (net) of Rs 10,670 lakhs (including Rs 1,075 lakhs recognised for the year) primarily on unused business losses. Having incurred losses in the current year and lacking sufficient appropriate audit evidence for management's future-profitability assumptions, the auditors were unable to comment on the reliability of the profit projections or the timing and quantum of future taxable profits, or to determine the effect on the DTA carrying value and the loss for the year. Recovery of this asset depends entirely on TIL delivering the taxable profits it has yet to demonstrate.

risks.risk: Sustained loss-making record and unproven turnaround
risks.note: Loss before tax for FY26 was Rs (40.64) crore against a profit of Rs 4.15 crore in the previous year, and the Directors' Report states that 'persistent lack of business performance had resulted in significant losses over the years'. The revival is only about 24 months old, so the earnings base supporting the whole investment case is still an expectation rather than a track record.

risks.risk: Execution lag on localisation and new-product design engineering
risks.note: Management states that crucial revival processes - localisation of critical imported componentry and design engineering of newer products - 'have not yet yielded full results' and by their nature need more time to reflect in operational performance. Until localisation lands, the cost structure remains exposed to imported componentry and to forex and supply-chain disruption; the 'steep' profitable-growth trajectory directors expect is contingent on these steps working.

risks.risk: Dependence on foreign OEM alliances for a core part of the portfolio
risks.note: A material share of the product range - Grove mobile cranes and Manitowoc crawler cranes, and Hyster lift trucks and port-handling systems - is sold under fixed-term arrangements with foreign principals (exclusive Manitowoc partnership since 1994; a renewed five-year Dealer Sales & Service Agreement with Hyster-Yale Asia-Pacific effective June 2024). Continuity of these agreements, and the terms on which they renew, sit outside TIL's control.

The order book stood at approximately Rs 274 crore as of March 2026 (Orders in Hand ~Rs 116.7 crore, pipeline ~Rs 157.1 crore) and the roughly Rs 200 crore of new FY26 orders came principally from two counterparties - CONCOR and the Indian Armed Forces. Revenue visibility therefore rests on a small number of large, lumpy, government-linked relationships whose ordering cycles and tender outcomes can move sharply.

risks.risk: Self-identified ESG and control gaps from the FY25 gap assessment
risks.note: The ESG advisory gap assessment identified an absence of a formal environment policy and monitoring gaps for hazardous waste and energy use; gaps in health & safety systems, employment records and inclusion practices; and governance gaps in climate risk assessment, anti-corruption documentation and infrastructure investment records. These are disclosed control weaknesses in a heavy-engineering operation, with GRI-aligned reporting only targeted for FY27.

risks.risk: Reliance on the promoter and Gainwell Group ecosystem for funding and operations
risks.note: Growth funding required strengthening net worth through share warrants convertible into equity of up to Rs 60 crore issued to promoter TIL Global Private Limited on a preferential basis, and the related-party note shows loans from the holding company (TIL Global), an interest-free loan from ultimate holding company Indocrest Transportation, advances and shared manpower arrangements with Gainwell group entities, and the purchase of the 60% TCPL stake from Gainwell Commosales. Balance-sheet and operating dependence on connected parties concentrates governance and funding risk in one group.

risks.risk: Integration and diversification risk in newly entered adjacencies
risks.note: TIL is simultaneously entering clean energy engineering through the 60% acquisition of Tulip Compression Private Limited (CNG, LNG and Hydrogen compression and dispensing, effective 7 May 2026) and scaling a dedicated defence SBU, while running an in-flight SAP ERP implementation across its facilities. Multiple concurrent step-changes in a company still restoring profitability raise the odds of execution slippage.

hero.oneLiner: TIL positions itself as an 80-year-old Indian material handling and infrastructure equipment leader transforming into a diversified, indigenous capital goods engineering group spanning material handling, defence and clean energy through the acquisition of Tulip Compression (TCPL).

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Established in 1944, TIL is described as India's leading material handling and infrastructure equipment manufacturer, headquartered in Kolkata with a pan-India presence, ISO 9001:2015 certified and holding strategic alliances with international industry leaders.
- With TCPL now in the fold, TIL frames itself as a diversified, indigenous capital goods engineering company spanning defence, material handling and clean energy (CNG, LNG and Hydrogen engineering solutions).
- TIL is regaining its stronghold in the Reach Stacker segment and is targeting a 38%-40% market share in the coming year.
- TCPL is positioned as a fast-growing clean energy solutions provider with a formidable presence across India's City Gas Distribution (CGD) industry.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body: - [Acquisition] Tulip Compression Private Limited (TCPL) became a majority-owned subsidiary of TIL in May 2026, with its synergistic integration into TIL described as successfully completed; TCPL's results were consolidated into TIL's financials for part of Q1FY27.
